headline: Maton's pinch-hit single in the ninth walks off Reds
recap: Trailing 6-5 entering the bottom of the ninth after Cincinnati retook the lead in the top half, the Phillies rallied to beat the Reds 7-6 at Citizens Bank Park. Jean Segura led off the inning with a walk against Reds closer Alexis Diaz. Pinch-hitter Bryson Stott, batting for Yairo Munoz, ripped a double to center field, and center fielder Nick Senzel's throw toward third got away for an error, letting Segura race home from first to tie the game at 6 while Stott took third on the miscue. Pinch-hitter Nick Maton, batting for Edmundo Sosa, then singled to right field to score Stott and end the game.

Ranger Suarez started for the Phillies and allowed three earned runs on six hits over 5 2/3 innings with five strikeouts and four walks. Reds starter Nick Lodolo worked 5 1/3 innings and was charged with four earned runs on three hits, striking out five and walking two.

Philadelphia scored four runs in the sixth to take a 4-3 lead, capped by J.T. Realmuto's two-run triple that scored Rhys Hoskins and Alec Bohm and Nick Castellanos's single that brought home Realmuto. Matt Vierling led off the seventh with a solo home run, his fifth of the season, to make it 5-3. Cincinnati cut the deficit to 5-4 in the eighth on Aristides Aquino's RBI double, then took a 6-5 lead in the ninth when TJ Friedl tripled off Brad Hand, scoring Nick Senzel and Kyle Farmer. Hand was credited with the win despite allowing the go-ahead runs, and Alexis Diaz took the loss.
